cards.en:
Intuition: name is the label on a box. The server finds the data by its label.

  • When submitted, each field is sent as a name=value pair.
  • In PHP, the name becomes the index: name="age" → $_POST["age"].
  • A field without a name is not sent.
  • Names are case-sensitive: Age ≠ age.

Exam wording: The name attribute provides the key (index) used to identify the field's value in the request, e.g. $_POST["age"].
cards.zh:
直觉：name 是箱子上的标签，服务器靠它找数据。

  • 提交时每个字段以 name=value 送出。
  • PHP 中 name 就是 index：$_POST["age"]。
  • 没有 name 的字段不会被送出。
  • 区分大小写。

考试写法：The name attribute provides the key (index) used to identify the field's value in the request, e.g. $_POST["age"].

ex.q: Field <input type="text" name="city">; user types Tokyo; method GET. Query string?
ex.a:
1. Pair = name=value.
2. ?city=Tokyo.

ex.q: How does PHP read it if method is POST?
ex.a: $city = $_POST["city"]; → "Tokyo".

ex.q: Field has id="city" but no name. PHP reads $_POST["city"]. Result?
ex.a:
1. id is for CSS/JS only.
2. Without name, nothing is sent.
3. PHP gives an undefined index warning. Fix: add name="city".
ex.az: id 不会送出；无 name → undefined index。要加 name。

code.src:
<?php
$city = $_POST["city"];
echo "You chose {$city}";
?>

notes.tz: 读取 name 为 city 的值

cards.en:
Intuition: required is a doorman who won't let an empty form leave the browser.

  • Add required to a field: the browser blocks submission if it is empty and shows a message.
  • It is a client-side presence check: fast, no server trip.
  • But users can remove it (developer tools) or send requests directly, so the server must still check.

Exam wording: The required attribute performs a client-side presence check; it can be bypassed, so server-side validation is still needed.
cards.zh:
直觉：required 像门卫，空表单不准离开浏览器。

  • 字段加 required：空白时浏览器阻止提交并提示。
  • 属 client-side presence check，快、不用经服务器。
  • 但可被绕过（开发者工具或直接送请求），服务器仍要检查。

考试写法：The required attribute performs a client-side presence check; it can be bypassed, so server-side validation is still needed.

ex.q: Make the email field compulsory.
ex.a: <input type="text" name="email" required> (a Boolean attribute: no value needed).

ex.q: User leaves it blank and clicks submit. What happens?
ex.a:
1. Browser checks first.
2. Shows 'Please fill in this field'.
3. No request is sent.
ex.az: 浏览器提示，不发出请求。

ex.q: 'With required, my PHP needn't check empty input.' Right?
ex.a:
1. A user can delete the attribute in dev tools.
2. Or send a request without the form.
3. Wrong: always check with empty() in PHP too.
ex.az: 可被绕过，PHP 仍要用 empty() 检查。

code.src:
<form onsubmit="alert('sent');return false">
  <input type="text" name="email" required>
  <input type="submit">
</form>

notes.t: Demo form (alert instead of real send)

demo.html:
<form onsubmit="alert('sent');return false">
  Email: <input type="text" name="email" required>
  <input type="submit">
</form>

cards.en:
Intuition: like covering your PIN at an ATM: people behind you see only dots.

  • <input type="password" name="pw"> shows dots instead of letters.
  • It only hides on screen. The value is sent as normal text.
  • With GET, the password would appear in the URL, so use POST (and HTTPS for real security).

Exam wording: A password field masks the characters on screen, but it does not encrypt the data; use POST and HTTPS.
cards.zh:
直觉：像在 ATM 遮住密码，旁人只见圆点。

  • type="password" 以圆点显示。
  • 只在屏幕上隐藏，送出时仍是普通文字。
  • 用 GET 会在 URL 显示密码，要用 POST（真正安全要 HTTPS）。

考试写法：A password field masks the characters on screen, but it does not encrypt the data; use POST and HTTPS.

ex.q: Write a login form with username and password.
ex.a:
1. <form action="login.php" method="POST">
2. <input type="text" name="user">
3. <input type="password" name="pw">
4. Submit button, close form.

ex.q: A login form uses GET; user enters pw abc123. What's in the URL?
ex.a: login.php?user=tom&pw=abc123, visible in history. Bad; use POST.
ex.az: 密码出现在 URL；应用 POST。

ex.q: 'The password field encrypts the password.' True?
ex.a:
1. It only masks on screen.
2. Data is plain text in the request.
3. False; encryption needs HTTPS.

code.src: Password: <input type="password" name="pw">

demo.html: Password:

cards.en:
Intuition: a calendar picker stops people typing '31 Feb'.

  • <input type="date" name="d"> shows a date picker.
  • The value is sent as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-12-01.
  • min and max limit the range: min="2026-12-01" max="2026-12-31".
  • Because the format is YYYY-MM-DD, PHP can compare dates as strings.

Exam wording: The min and max attributes perform a client-side range check on the date.
cards.zh:
直觉：日历选择器防止输入“2 月 31 日”。

  • type="date" 显示日期选择器。
  • 送出格式 YYYY-MM-DD。
  • min/max 限制范围。
  • 格式统一，PHP 可直接用字符串比较日期。

考试写法：The min and max attributes perform a client-side range check on the date.

ex.q: Booking only in December 2026. Write the field.
ex.a: <input type="date" name="bday" min="2026-12-01" max="2026-12-31">

ex.q: User picks 5 Jan 2027. Which value is sent?
ex.a:
1. Format YYYY-MM-DD.
2. Sent: bday=2027-01-05.

ex.q: A student writes min="01/12/2026". Problem?
ex.a:
1. min must use YYYY-MM-DD.
2. The wrong format is ignored, so no limit.
3. Fix: min="2026-12-01".
ex.az: 格式错误会被忽略，应写 2026-12-01。

code.src: <input type="date" name="bday" min="2026-12-01" max="2026-12-31">

cards.en:
Intuition: a menu with fixed choices, so users can't type anything strange.

  • <select name="..."> holds several <option>.
  • Each option has a value (sent to the server) and display text (seen by user).
  • Only one option is sent: name=value of the chosen one.
  • selected makes an option the default.

Exam wording: A dropdown list restricts input to predefined options, which reduces input errors.
cards.zh:
直觉：固定选项的菜单，用户不能乱打。

  • <select name> 内有多个 <option>。
  • option 的 value 送到服务器，文字给用户看。
  • 只送出所选一项。
  • selected 设默认。

考试写法：A dropdown list restricts input to predefined options, which reduces input errors.

ex.q: Make a dropdown for form 4, 5, 6 with values S4, S5, S6.
ex.a: <select name="form"><option value="S4">Form 4</option><option value="S5">Form 5</option><option value="S6">Form 6</option></select>
ex.az: 三个 option，value 分别为 S4/S5/S6。

ex.q: User picks 'Form 5'. What does $_POST["form"] hold?
ex.a: The option's value: "S5", not "Form 5".

ex.q: A student puts name on each <option> instead of <select>. Effect?
ex.a:
1. Only <select>'s name is used.
2. Nothing is sent. Fix: <select name="form">.
ex.az: name 要放在 select 上。

code.src:
<select name="form">
  <option value="S4">Form 4</option>
  <option value="S5" selected>Form 5</option>
  <option value="S6">Form 6</option>
</select>

demo.html: Sent: form=S5

cards.en:
Intuition: checkboxes are a shopping list: tick zero, one or many.

  • <input type="checkbox" name="fruit[]" value="apple">
  • Only ticked boxes are sent.
  • The [] after the name tells PHP to collect all ticked values into an array: $_POST["fruit"] = ["apple","pear"].
  • If nothing is ticked, the index does not exist, so test with isset().

Exam wording: Use name[] so that multiple selected values are received as an array.
cards.zh:
直觉：checkbox 像购物清单，可勾零个、一个或多个。

  • 只有被勾选的会送出。
  • 名字后加 []，PHP 会把所有值收成 array。
  • 全不勾 → index 不存在，要用 isset()。

考试写法：Use name[] so that multiple selected values are received as an array.

ex.q: Boxes apple, pear, kiwi (name fruit[]); user ticks apple and kiwi. Value of $_POST["fruit"]?
ex.a:
1. Only ticked ones are sent.
2. Array: ["apple", "kiwi"]; count is 2.

ex.q: Same form, nothing ticked. Is isset($_POST["fruit"]) true?
ex.a: No. No pair is sent, so the index is missing → false.

ex.q: Names written as name="fruit" (no []). User ticks apple and kiwi. Result?
ex.a:
1. Both send fruit=…
2. The later one overwrites: $_POST["fruit"] = "kiwi" only.
3. Fix: use fruit[].
ex.az: 没有 [] 时后者覆盖，只剩 kiwi。

code.src: "; } } else { echo "None"; } ?>

notes.t: Was at least one box ticked?
Loop over the array of ticked values
Print each value on its own line

cards.en:
Intuition: the 'post' button that sends the envelope.

  • <input type="submit" name="submit" value="Calculate">
  • value = text on the button.
  • If it has a name, the button itself is sent too (submit=Calculate). PHP can test isset($_POST["submit"]) to know the form was submitted.

Exam wording: Clicking the submit button sends the form data to the URL in the action attribute.
cards.zh:
直觉：把信封寄出的按钮。

  • value 是按钮文字。
  • 有 name 时按钮本身也会送出（submit=Calculate），PHP 可用 isset($_POST["submit"]) 判断表单是否已提交。

考试写法：Clicking the submit button sends the form data to the URL in the action attribute.

ex.q: Make a button that shows 'Go!'.
ex.a: <input type="submit" value="Go!">

ex.q: Form has a=3 and button name="submit" value="Calc", POST. List the sent pairs.
ex.a: a=3&submit=Calc

ex.q: Button has no name, but PHP checks isset($_POST["submit"]). What goes wrong?
ex.a:
1. Without a name, the button isn't sent.
2. isset is always false, so results never show.
3. Fix: add name="submit".
ex.az: 没有 name 不会送出，isset 永远 false。

code.src: <input type="submit" name="submit" value="Calculate">

demo.html: a:

cards.tz: Number 字段与 step 属性
cards.en:
Intuition: a box that only accepts numbers, with arrows to go up and down.

  • <input type="number" name="qty" min="1" max="10">
  • step = allowed jump. Default step="1", so 2.5 is rejected.
  • step="0.1" allows one decimal place; step="any" allows any decimal.
  • The value still reaches PHP as a string (e.g. "2.5").

Exam wording: type="number" performs a client-side type check; step="any" allows decimal values.
cards.zh:
直觉：只收数字的格子，有上下箭头。

  • step 是允许的间隔，默认 1，所以 2.5 会被拒。
  • step="0.1" 一位小数；step="any" 任意小数。
  • 到 PHP 时仍是字符串。

考试写法：type="number" performs a client-side type check; step="any" allows decimal values.

ex.q: Weight in kg with decimals, 1–300.
ex.a: <input type="number" name="w" min="1" max="300" step="any">

ex.q: step="5" min="0": which of 10, 12, 15 are allowed?
Height field has no step; user enters 1.75. Why is it rejected?
ex.a:
1. Default step is 1.
2. 1.75 isn't a whole-number step.
3. Fix: step="any" or step="0.01".

code.src: <input type="number" name="h" step="any" min="0.5" max="2.5">

notes.t: Height in metres; any decimal from 0.5 to 2.5

demo.html:
step=1:

Try 1.75: browser rejects it. Change step to any to allow it.

cards.t: Example 3.1 method: building a form from a wireframe
cards.tz: 例 3.1 方法：按 wireframe 建表单
cards.en:
Intuition: a wireframe is a sketch. You turn each box in the sketch into one field.

  1. List every input in the wireframe.
  2. Choose the best type for each (text, password, number, date, select, checkbox).
  3. Give each a clear name (and [] for checkboxes).
  4. Add checks: required, min/max, step.
  5. Wrap in <form action method> and add a submit button.

Exam wording: Choose input types that restrict the data entered, to reduce input errors.
cards.zh:
直觉：wireframe 是草图，把每个格子变成一个字段。

  1. 列出所有输入。
  2. 选最合适的 type。
  3. 给每个字段 name（checkbox 加 []）。
  4. 加检查：required、min/max、step。
  5. 包进 <form> 并加 submit。

考试写法：Choose input types that restrict the data entered, to reduce input errors.

ex.q: Wireframe: Name, Gender (M/F), Date of birth, Hobbies (several). Choose types.
ex.a:
1. Name → text, required.
2. Gender → select (2 fixed options).
3. DOB → date.
4. Hobbies → checkbox with hobby[].

ex.q: Number of tickets 1–4, whole numbers. Field?
ex.a: <input type="number" name="tix" min="1" max="4" required>

ex.q: A student uses a text field for date of birth. Why is this weak?
ex.a:
1. Users can type '31/02' or 'abc'.
2. Formats vary.
3. Better: type="date" gives a valid YYYY-MM-DD.

code.src:
Name:
Gender:
DOB:
Music Sport

notes.t: Form sent to join.php by POST
Dropdown; without value attr the text is sent
notes.tz: 没有 value 时送出文字

demo.html:
Name:
Gender:
DOB:
Music Sport

cards.t: Submitting a form: the four steps
cards.en:
Intuition: like posting a letter: write it, put it in an envelope, address it, post it.

  1. User clicks submit.
  2. Browser collects every named field as name=value pairs.
  3. Browser builds an HTTP request to the action URL using the method (GET: pairs in the URL query string; POST: pairs in the request body).
  4. Server runs the script and sends back an HTTP response (the new HTML page).

Exam wording: The browser encodes the form data as name-value pairs and sends them in an HTTP request to the URL specified in the action attribute.
cards.zh:
直觉：像寄信：写好、装信封、写地址、寄出。

  1. 用户按 submit。
  2. 浏览器把有 name 的字段收集成 name=value。
  3. 按 method 向 action URL 发出 HTTP request（GET 放 URL；POST 放 body）。
  4. 服务器执行 script，回传 HTML。

考试写法：The browser encodes the form data as name-value pairs and sends them in an HTTP request to the URL specified in the action attribute.

ex.q: Form action="bmi.php" method GET, fields w=60, h=1.7. Write the request URL.
ex.a:
1. Pairs: w=60, h=1.7.
2. Join with &, add after ?
3. bmi.php?w=60&h=1.7

ex.q: Same form with POST. Where is the data?
ex.a: In the request body: w=60&h=1.7. URL is just bmi.php.
ex.az: 在 request body，URL 只是 bmi.php。

ex.q: 'The browser calculates the BMI when submit is clicked.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. The browser only packs and sends data.
2. bmi.php on the server calculates.
3. Wrong.
ex.az: 浏览器只送数据，服务器计算。

frames.en: User clicks Submit.
Browser builds w=60&h=1.7 from named fields.
GET bmi.php?w=60&h=1.7 is sent.
Server returns HTML with the BMI.

cards.en:
Intuition: the query string is a note stuck on the end of the URL.

  • Starts with ? after the file path.
  • Pairs written as name=value.
  • Pairs separated by &.
  • Special characters are encoded: space → + or %20; @ → %40.
  • Checkbox arrays repeat the name: c[]=a&c[]=b.

Exam wording: With GET, form data is appended to the URL as a query string: ?name1=value1&name2=value2.
cards.zh:
直觉：query string 是贴在 URL 后的便条。

  • 以 ? 开始。
  • 每对 name=value。
  • 用 & 分隔。
  • 特殊字符要编码：空格 → + 或 %20。
  • checkbox 数组会重复名字。

考试写法：With GET, form data is appended to the URL as a query string: ?name1=value1&name2=value2.

ex.q: Fields name="Tom Ho", age=16 to find.php by GET. URL?
ex.a:
1. Encode space: Tom+Ho.
2. find.php?name=Tom+Ho&age=16

ex.q: URL shop.php?item=pen&qty=3. What is $_GET["qty"]?
ex.a: "3" (a string).

ex.q: A student writes find.php&name=Tom?age=16. What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. ? must come first, then & between pairs.
2. Correct: find.php?name=Tom&age=16.

code.src:
const p = new URLSearchParams({name: "Tom Ho", age: 16});
console.log("find.php?" + p.toString());

notes.t: Build pairs like a browser does
notes.tz: 像浏览器那样建立 name=value

demo.src:
const p = new URLSearchParams({name: "Tom Ho", age: 16});
console.log("find.php?" + p.toString());

cards.t: Misconception: who chooses GET or POST?
cards.tz: 误解：谁决定 GET 或 POST？
cards.en:
Intuition: the shop prints the order slip; the customer just fills it in.

  • The developer chooses GET or POST by writing the method attribute.
  • The user cannot choose; they only click submit.
  • If no method is given, the browser uses GET by default.

Exam wording: The HTTP method is specified by the developer in the method attribute of the form element.
cards.zh:
直觉：订单是店家印的，客人只负责填。

  • 开发者在 method 属性决定 GET 或 POST。
  • 用户不能选，只是按 submit。
  • 没写 method 时默认 GET。

考试写法：The HTTP method is specified by the developer in the method attribute of the form element.

ex.q: Form tag: <form action="a.php">. Which method is used?
ex.a: No method attribute → default GET.

ex.q: 'The user decides to use POST for privacy.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Users cannot change the method in a normal form.
2. It's set by the developer.
3. Wrong.

ex.q: How would a developer switch to POST?
ex.a: Edit the tag: <form action="a.php" method="POST">, and read $_POST instead of $_GET in PHP.
ex.az: 改 method 并在 PHP 用 $_POST。

cards.tz: GET 与 POST 的意图
cards.en:
Intuition: GET = asking a question; POST = handing in something that changes things.

GETPOST
PurposeRetrieve dataSend/change data on server
Examplessearch, filtersign up, order, upload
Repeat safe?YesMay repeat the action (e.g. order twice)

Exam wording: GET is used to request/retrieve data; POST is used to submit data that changes the state of the server (e.g. insert a record).
cards.zh:
直觉：GET 是问问题；POST 是交东西改变服务器。

GETPOST
用途取得数据提交/更改数据
例子搜寻注册、下单、上载
重复安全可能重复动作

考试写法：GET is used to request/retrieve data; POST is used to submit data that changes the state of the server (e.g. insert a record).

ex.q: A library search box. GET or POST?
ex.a: Only retrieves book data → GET.

ex.q: Placing an online order. GET or POST?
ex.a: Creates a new record on the server → POST.

ex.q: A student uses GET for 'delete my account'. Why bad?
ex.a:
1. GET should not change data.
2. The URL could be bookmarked/reopened or prefetched and delete again.
3. Use POST.
ex.az: GET 不应改数据，应用 POST。

cards.t: GET vs POST: visibility, bookmarks and history
cards.tz: GET 与 POST：可见性、书签、历史
cards.en:
Intuition: GET writes the data on the outside of the envelope; POST puts it inside.

GETPOST
Data shown in URL?YesNo (in body)
Bookmark / share results?YesNo
Stored in browser history?YesNo
For passwords?NeverYes (with HTTPS)

Exam wording: GET data is visible in the URL and saved in browser history, so it is unsuitable for sensitive data; however, the result page can be bookmarked.
cards.zh:
直觉：GET 把数据写在信封外，POST 放在里面。

GETPOST
URL 可见是否
可书签/分享可不可
历史记录有无
密码不可可（配 HTTPS）

考试写法：GET data is visible in the URL and saved in browser history, so it is unsuitable for sensitive data; however, the result page can be bookmarked.

ex.q: A user wants to share search results for 'laptop' with a friend. Which method helps?
ex.a: GET: URL search.php?q=laptop can be copied and shared.

ex.q: Login form on a shared school computer uses GET. Risk?
ex.a:
1. Password appears in URL.
2. Saved in history; next user can see it.
3. Use POST.
ex.az: 密码留在历史，应用 POST。

ex.q: 'POST data is encrypted, so it's secure.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. POST only hides data from the URL.
2. It is still plain text on the network.
3. Wrong; HTTPS encrypts.

cards.t: GET vs POST: size, data type and caching
cards.tz: GET 与 POST：大小、数据类型、缓存
cards.en:
Intuition: a URL is a short sticky note; the body is a big box.

GETPOST
SizeLimited (URL length, a few KB)Much larger
Data typeText (ASCII) onlyText and binary (files)
Cached?Can be cachedNot cached normally

Exam wording: POST should be used for large data or file uploads because GET is limited by the URL length and only supports ASCII characters.
cards.zh:
直觉：URL 是小便条，body 是大箱子。

GETPOST
大小有限大得多
类型只限 ASCII 文字文字及二进制（文件）
缓存可缓存通常不缓存

考试写法：POST should be used for large data or file uploads because GET is limited by the URL length and only supports ASCII characters.

ex.q: Uploading a profile photo: method?
ex.a: A photo is binary and large → POST.

ex.q: A 5000-word essay form: method?
ex.a: Long text may exceed URL limit → POST.

ex.q: 'GET is faster, so always use GET.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Caching can speed up repeated GETs.
2. But GET can't carry files or long data and exposes data.
3. Wrong: choose by purpose.
ex.az: 按用途选择，不是一律 GET。

cards.t: Example 3.2 method: choosing GET or POST
cards.tz: 例 3.2 方法：选择 GET 或 POST
cards.en:
Intuition: ask four quick questions.

  1. Does it change server data? → POST.
  2. Is it sensitive (password, ID)? → POST.
  3. Is it large or a file? → POST.
  4. Should users bookmark/share the result? → GET.

If none apply (simple retrieval) → GET.

Exam wording: state the choice and one reason linked to the scenario, e.g. POST, because the password should not be shown in the URL.
cards.zh:
直觉：问四个问题。

  1. 会更改服务器数据？→ POST。
  2. 敏感？→ POST。
  3. 大或文件？→ POST。
  4. 想书签/分享结果？→ GET。

都不是 → GET。

考试写法：写出选择及与情境相关的理由，如 POST, because the password should not be shown in the URL.

ex.q: Weather lookup by district.
ex.a: Retrieval, not sensitive, shareable → GET, so the page for a district can be bookmarked.

ex.q: Changing account password.
ex.a: Sensitive + changes data → POST.

ex.q: Answer given: 'POST, because it is better.' Why does it get 0 marks?
ex.a:
1. No link to the scenario.
2. Must give a reason, e.g. 'the HKID number would be shown in the URL with GET'.

cards.t: Server side of the request-response cycle
cards.en:
Intuition: the kitchen side of the restaurant: take order, cook, serve.

  1. Web server receives the HTTP request for a .php file.
  2. PHP puts the form data into superglobal arrays ($_GET / $_POST).
  3. The PHP interpreter runs the script, which reads the data, validates, and computes.
  4. Output becomes the resulting HTML, sent in the HTTP response.

Exam wording: The server-side script retrieves the form data from $_GET or $_POST, processes it, and generates HTML in the HTTP response.
cards.zh:
直觉：餐厅厨房：接单、煮、上菜。

  1. 服务器接收 .php 请求。
  2. PHP 把表单数据放入 superglobal（$_GET / $_POST）。
  3. PHP interpreter 执行 script：读取、验证、计算。
  4. 输出成为 resulting HTML 回传。

考试写法：The server-side script retrieves the form data from $_GET or $_POST, processes it, and generates HTML in the HTTP response.

ex.q: Request hi.php?n=Amy; hi.php has echo "Hi ".$_GET["n"];. Response body?
ex.a:
1. $_GET["n"] = "Amy".
2. Output: Hi Amy.

ex.q: Which runs first: validation or calculation?
ex.a: Validation, so that bad data never reaches the calculation.

ex.q: 'The server sends the PHP file to the browser to run.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. The server runs PHP itself.
2. Only HTML is sent.
3. Wrong.
ex.az: 服务器自己执行，只送 HTML。

frames.en: Request arrives: POST bmi.php with w, h.
Validate, then BMI = 60/1.7² ≈ 20.76.
HTML 'Your BMI is 20.76' sent back.

cards.en:
Intuition: two ready-made mailboxes that PHP fills before your code runs.

  • Superglobal = built-in variable available everywhere in the script.
  • $_GET: associative array of query-string data. $_POST: data from the request body.
  • Index = field name: $_POST["w"].
  • Every value is a string (checkbox[] → array of strings).
  • Must match the form's method: a POST form fills $_POST, not $_GET.

Exam wording: $_POST is an associative array containing the data sent by the POST method, indexed by the name attributes of the fields.
cards.zh:
直觉：两个现成信箱，代码执行前已装好数据。

  • Superglobal：内置、处处可用。
  • $_GET：query string 数据；$_POST：body 数据。
  • index = 字段 name。
  • 值都是字符串。
  • 要和 form method 对应。

考试写法：$_POST is an associative array containing the data sent by the POST method, indexed by the name attributes of the fields.

ex.q: URL p.php?x=4&y=5. Write PHP to print x+y.
ex.a:
1. $x = $_GET["x"]; $y = $_GET["y"];
2. echo $x + $y; → 9 (numeric strings convert).

ex.q: What is the type of $_POST["age"] when the user typed 16?
ex.a: String "16".

ex.q: Form method="POST" but PHP uses $_GET["w"]. Result?
ex.a:
1. Data is in $_POST.
2. $_GET["w"] is undefined → warning, blank value.
3. Fix: use $_POST.

code.src:
<?php
$x = $_GET["x"];
$y = $_GET["y"];
echo "Sum: " . ($x + $y);
?>

notes.t: Read x from the URL query string

cards.t: Using $_POST values inside strings and calculations
cards.tz: 在字符串和计算中使用 $_POST
cards.en:
Intuition: copy the value into a simple variable first; it's easier to read and use.

  • Assign: $w = $_POST["w"];
  • Inside double quotes, wrap array elements in curly braces: "Weight: {$_POST['w']} kg".
  • Arithmetic converts numeric strings automatically: "60" / 2 → 30.
  • round($x, 2) rounds to 2 decimal places.

Exam wording: Use {} to embed an array element in a double-quoted string.
cards.zh:
直觉：先把值复制到简单变量，好读好用。

  • $w = $_POST["w"];
  • 双引号内放数组元素要用花括号："{$_POST['w']}"。
  • 运算时数字字符串会自动转换。
  • round($x,2) 取两位小数。

考试写法：Use {} to embed an array element in a double-quoted string.

ex.q: w="60". Output of echo "Half: " . $_POST["w"]/2;?
ex.a:
1. / runs before . (higher precedence in PHP 8).
2. 60/2 = 30 → Half: 30.

ex.q: Print 'Hello Amy!' where name is in $_POST["n"].
ex.a: echo "Hello {$_POST['n']}!";

ex.q: A student writes echo "Hi $_POST["n"]";. Problem?
ex.a:
1. The inner double quotes end the string early → syntax error.
2. Fix: "Hi {$_POST['n']}" or "Hi " . $_POST["n"].
ex.az: 内部双引号令字符串提早结束。

code.src:
<?php
$w = $_POST["w"];
$h = $_POST["h"];
$bmi = round($w / ($h * $h), 2);
echo "Weight {$_POST['w']} kg, BMI {$bmi}";
?>

cards.en:
Intuition: a full mini-app: a form page and a result page.

  • bmi.html: form, action="bmi.php" method="POST", fields w and h (number, step="any").
  • bmi.php: reads $_POST, computes BMI = weight / height², classifies, and echoes HTML.
  • Classification uses if-elseif-else (e.g. <18.5 underweight, <23 normal, else overweight, local guideline).

Exam wording: The PHP script retrieves the weight and height from $_POST, calculates the BMI and outputs it as HTML.
cards.zh:
直觉：完整小应用：表单页 + 结果页。

  • bmi.html：POST 到 bmi.php，字段 w、h。
  • bmi.php：读 $_POST，计算 BMI = 体重/身高²，分类并输出 HTML。
  • 用 if-elseif-else 分类。

考试写法：The PHP script retrieves the weight and height from $_POST, calculates the BMI and outputs it as HTML.

ex.q: w=45, h=1.6. Output?
w=70, h=1.75. Output?
A student writes $bmi = $w / $h * $h;. w=60, h=1.7 gives 60. Why?
ex.a:
1. / and * same precedence, left to right: (60/1.7)*1.7 = 60.
2. Fix: $w / ($h * $h) or $w / $h ** 2.

code.src:
BMI {$bmi}: {$c}

"; ?>

demo.html:
Weight (kg):
Height (m):

(This preview uses JavaScript to imitate bmi.php.)

cards.en:
Intuition: client-side = a spell-checker on your phone; server-side = the teacher marking the paper. The teacher's check is the one that counts.

Client-sideServer-side
WhereBrowser (HTML attributes, JavaScript)Server (PHP)
SpeedInstant feedback, less server loadNeeds a round trip
Can be bypassed?YesNo
Can check against stored data?NoYes (e.g. email already registered)

Exam wording: Client-side validation gives immediate feedback and reduces server load; server-side validation cannot be bypassed and can check against data in the database.
cards.zh:
直觉：client-side 像手机拼字检查；server-side 像老师批改，后者才算数。

Client-sideServer-side
位置浏览器服务器（PHP）
速度即时回馈，减轻服务器负担要来回一次
可绕过可以不可
可对照已存数据不可可以

考试写法：Client-side validation gives immediate feedback and reduces server load; server-side validation cannot be bypassed and can check against data in the database.

ex.q: Give one advantage of client-side validation.
ex.a: Immediate feedback without sending a request, so less network traffic and server load.

ex.q: Checking a username is not already taken: which side?
ex.a:
1. Needs the list of existing users.
2. That list is in the server database.
3. → server-side.

ex.q: 'Client-side validation is enough because the form has required.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Users can edit HTML or send requests directly.
2. Wrong: server-side validation is always needed.

cards.t: Misconception: validation is one or the other; always validate on the server
cards.en:
Intuition: a seat belt and an airbag: use both.

  • Good apps use both: client-side for user convenience, server-side for safety.
  • Never trust data from the client: it can be tampered with (dev tools, scripts, tools like curl).
  • The server is the last line of defence.

Exam wording: Server-side validation must still be done because client-side validation can be bypassed by modifying the HTML or sending the HTTP request directly.
cards.zh:
直觉：安全带和气囊，两样都要。

  • 好的应用两者都用：client-side 方便，server-side 安全。
  • 客户端数据可被篡改。
  • 服务器是最后防线。

考试写法：Server-side validation must still be done because client-side validation can be bypassed by modifying the HTML or sending the HTTP request directly.

ex.q: A form has max="10" for quantity. How could a user still send 999?
ex.a:
1. Open dev tools, delete max.
2. Or type order.php?qty=999 (if GET).
3. The server receives 999.
ex.az: 删除 max 或直接改 URL。

ex.q: So what should order.php do?
ex.a: Check again: if ($_GET["qty"] < 1 || $_GET["qty"] > 10) { $valid = false; }

ex.q: 'If we validate on the server, client-side checks are useless.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Client-side still gives instant feedback.
2. It reduces bad requests.
3. Wrong: both have value.

cards.en:
Intuition: a traffic light that starts green; any failed check turns it red.

  1. Set $valid = true;
  2. Run each check; if one fails, set $valid = false; (and maybe store a message).
  3. At the end: if ($valid) { process } else { show error }.

A flag is a Boolean variable that records whether something happened.

Exam wording: A flag variable is initialised to true and set to false when any validation check fails; the data is processed only if the flag remains true.
cards.zh:
直觉：交通灯先是绿色，任何检查失败就转红。

  1. $valid = true;
  2. 逐项检查，失败就 $valid = false;
  3. 最后 if ($valid) 才处理。

flag 是记录某事是否发生的 Boolean 变量。

考试写法：A flag variable is initialised to true and set to false when any validation check fails; the data is processed only if the flag remains true.

ex.q: name="" and age="15". Trace the code below.
ex.a:
1. $valid = true.
2. empty("") true → $valid = false.
3. age check passes.
4. Output: Invalid input.

ex.q: name="Amy", age="abc". Output?
ex.a: is_numeric("abc") false → $valid = false → Invalid input.

ex.q: A student writes $valid = true; inside each check (when it passes). Bug?
ex.a:
1. A later passing check resets it to true.
2. A failed earlier check is forgotten.
3. Only ever set it to false after the start.
ex.az: 通过时不要设回 true，否则会覆盖之前的失败。

code.src:
<?php
$valid = true;
if (empty($_POST["name"])) { $valid = false; }
if (!is_numeric($_POST["age"])) { $valid = false; }
if ($valid) { echo "Welcome {$_POST['name']}"; }
else { echo "Invalid input"; }
?>

cards.en:
Intuition: isset asks 'is there a box?'; empty asks 'is the box empty or zero?'.

Valueisset()empty()
index missingfalsetrue
""truetrue
"0"truetrue (!)
"abc"truefalse
  • isset(): variable/index exists and is not null.
  • empty(): missing, "", "0", 0, null, false, or empty array.

Exam wording: empty() is used for a presence check; note that empty("0") returns true.
cards.zh:
直觉：isset 问“有没有盒子”；empty 问“盒子是否空或零”。

值isset()empty()
不存在falsetrue
""truetrue
"0"truetrue
"abc"truefalse

考试写法：empty() is used for a presence check; note that empty("0") returns true.

ex.q: Text field left blank and submitted. isset? empty?
ex.a:
1. Text fields are always sent, value "".
2. isset → true; empty → true. So use empty() for presence.

ex.q: Unticked checkbox group. isset($_POST["c"])?
ex.a: Not sent at all → false.

ex.q: Quantity field: user enters 0; code uses empty() and says 'missing'. Why?
ex.a:
1. empty("0") is true.
2. Fix: $_POST["q"] === "" or strlen(...) == 0 for presence.

code.src:
<?php
$a = "0";
var_dump(isset($a));
var_dump(empty($a));
var_dump(empty("abc"));
?>

cards.t: Validation functions: presence, fixed value, type
cards.en:
Intuition: each check is a simple question about the input.

CheckQuestionPHP
PresenceWas something entered?!empty($x)
Fixed valueIs it one of allowed values?$x == "M" || $x == "F" or in_array($x, $list)
TypeIs it a number?is_numeric($x)

Exam wording: name the check and give the condition, e.g. type check: is_numeric($_POST["age"]) must be true.
cards.zh:
直觉：每种检查是一个简单问题。

检查问题PHP
Presence有没有输入!empty($x)
Fixed value是否允许的值in_array
Type是否数字is_numeric

考试写法：写出检查名称和条件，如 type check: is_numeric($_POST["age"]) must be true.

ex.q: Gender must be M or F. Code?
ex.a: if (!in_array($_POST["g"], ["M","F"])) { $valid = false; }

ex.q: is_numeric of "12.5", "1e3", "12a"?
ex.a: true, true, false.

ex.q: A student uses is_int($_POST["age"]) and it always fails. Why?
ex.a:
1. Form values are strings.
2. is_int("16") is false.
3. Use is_numeric (or ctype_digit for whole numbers).
ex.az: 表单值是字符串，is_int 永远 false。

code.src:
<?php
$g = "X"; $age = "12a";
echo in_array($g, ["M", "F"]) ? "ok" : "bad gender";
echo "\n";
echo is_numeric($age) ? "ok" : "bad age";
?>

cards.t: Length and format checks: strlen() and strpos()
cards.en:
Intuition: length = is it the right size; format = does it have the right shape.

  • strlen($s) returns the number of characters. Length check: strlen($pw) >= 8.
  • strpos($s, $find) returns the position (from 0) of the first match, or false if not found.
  • Format check for email: contains "@": strpos($e, "@") !== false.

Exam wording: Use !== false with strpos(), because position 0 is also a valid result.
cards.zh:
直觉：length 看长度；format 看形状。

  • strlen() 返回字符数。
  • strpos() 返回第一次出现的位置（由 0 起），找不到返回 false。
  • email 要有 @：strpos($e,"@") !== false。

考试写法：Use !== false with strpos(), because position 0 is also a valid result.

ex.q: strlen("Hello")?
strpos("tom@abc.com", "@")?
Code if (strpos($e, "@")) {...} with $e = "@abc". What goes wrong?
ex.a:
1. strpos returns 0.
2. 0 is treated as false, so a string that does contain @ fails.
3. Fix: !== false.
ex.az: 返回 0 被当 false，要用 !== false。

code.src:
<?php
$pw = "abc12";
echo strlen($pw) >= 8 ? "ok" : "too short";
echo "\n";
echo strpos("tom@abc.com", "@");
?>

cards.t: Date range check and loop presence check
cards.tz: 日期 range check 与循环 presence check
cards.en:
Intuition: dates in YYYY-MM-DD sort like words in a dictionary, so you can compare them as strings.

  • Range check: $d >= "2026-12-01" && $d <= "2026-12-31".
  • Loop presence check: put field names in an array and loop:
    foreach (["a","b","c"] as $f) { if (empty($_POST[$f])) $valid = false; }
  • Saves writing the same if many times.

Exam wording: Range check: the value must be between the lower and upper limits.
cards.zh:
直觉：YYYY-MM-DD 格式像字典排序，可以直接字符串比较。

  • Range check：$d >= "2026-12-01" && $d <= "2026-12-31"。
  • 循环 presence check：把字段名放入数组循环检查。

考试写法：Range check: the value must be between the lower and upper limits.

ex.q: $d = "2026-11-30". In December range?
Fields a="1", b="", c="3". Loop check result?
ex.a: b is empty → $valid = false.

ex.q: A student compares dates in DD/MM/YYYY strings: "05/01/2027" < "20/12/2026". Result and problem?
ex.a:
1. String compare: '0' < '2' → true, so Jan 2027 looks earlier.
2. Wrong. Use YYYY-MM-DD (as the date field sends).
ex.az: DD/MM 格式比较会错，用 YYYY-MM-DD。

code.src:
<?php
$valid = true;
foreach (["a", "b", "c"] as $f) {
  if (empty($_POST[$f])) { $valid = false; }
}
$d = $_POST["d"];
if ($d < "2026-12-01" || $d > "2026-12-31") { $valid = false; }
echo $valid ? "valid" : "invalid";
?>

cards.en:
Intuition: a cookie is like a cloakroom ticket: the website gives you a small ticket, and you show it every time you come back.

  • A Cookie is a small text file stored by a website in the client's browser.
  • It holds key-value pairs, e.g. lang=zh.
  • Uses: remember preferences (language, theme), keep users logged in, shopping carts, tracking.

Exam wording: A Cookie is a small piece of data stored in the client's browser by a website, sent back to the server in subsequent requests.
cards.zh:
直觉：Cookie 像衣帽间的票，每次回来都出示。

  • Cookie 是网站存放在用户浏览器的小文本文件。
  • 内含 key-value pair，如 lang=zh。
  • 用途：记住偏好、保持登入、购物车、追踪。

考试写法：A Cookie is a small piece of data stored in the client's browser by a website, sent back to the server in subsequent requests.

ex.q: Give two uses of cookies on a shopping site.
ex.a:
1. Remember items in the cart.
2. Remember the chosen language.

ex.q: Where is the cookie stored?
ex.a: On the client (in the browser), not on the server.

ex.q: 'Cookies are programs that can run on your computer.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Cookies are plain text data.
2. They cannot execute.
3. Wrong; the risk is privacy, not running code.
ex.az: Cookie 是文字数据，不能执行。

cards.t: How a Cookie is created and read
cards.en:
Intuition: server hands you a ticket once; your browser shows it automatically every visit.

  1. PHP calls setcookie("name", "value", expiry) before any output.
  2. The HTTP response carries a Set-Cookie header.
  3. Browser stores the cookie.
  4. In every later request to that site, the browser sends the cookie back.
  5. PHP reads it with $_COOKIE["name"].

To change it, send a new Set-Cookie with the same name. Note: $_COOKIE has the new value only from the next request.

Exam wording: The server attaches a set-cookie header to the HTTP response; the browser stores it and sends it in subsequent requests.
cards.zh:
直觉：服务器给你一次票，之后浏览器每次自动出示。

  1. setcookie()，要在任何输出之前。
  2. response 附 Set-Cookie header。
  3. 浏览器储存。
  4. 之后每次请求都送回。
  5. PHP 用 $_COOKIE["name"] 读取。

新值下一次请求才见于 $_COOKIE。

考试写法：The server attaches a set-cookie header to the HTTP response; the browser stores it and sends it in subsequent requests.

ex.q: Store GPA 3.8 for 30 days.
ex.a: setcookie("gpa", "3.8", time() + 30*24*60*60);

ex.q: Next visit: how to show it?
ex.a: echo $_COOKIE["gpa"]; → 3.8 (use isset first).

ex.q: Script calls setcookie() then immediately echoes $_COOKIE["gpa"] on the same first visit. Why is it undefined?
ex.a:
1. $_COOKIE holds cookies sent in this request.
2. The browser hasn't received/sent it yet.
3. Available on the next request.
ex.az: 本次请求未带 cookie，下次才有。

code.src:
<?php
if (isset($_COOKIE["gpa"])) {
  echo "Last GPA: " . $_COOKIE["gpa"];
} else {
  setcookie("gpa", "3.8", time() + 86400 * 30);
  echo "Cookie set";
}
?>

notes.t: Did the browser send a gpa cookie?
Ask browser to store gpa=3.8 for 30 days

frames.en: Browser requests gpa.php (no cookie).
Response includes Set-Cookie: gpa=3.8.
Browser saves the cookie for mysite.net.
Every request sends Cookie: gpa=3.8; PHP reads $_COOKIE["gpa"].

cards.en:
Intuition: a cinema's ticket only works at that cinema.

  • A cookie is linked to the domain that created it (e.g. mysite.net).
  • The browser sends it only to that domain.
  • Other websites cannot read it.
  • Cookies are also per browser: Chrome's cookies are not seen by Safari.

Exam wording: Cookies are domain-specific: a browser only sends a Cookie to the domain that created it.
cards.zh:
直觉：戏院票只能在那间戏院用。

  • cookie 与建立它的 domain 绑定。
  • 只送往该 domain。
  • 其他网站读不到。
  • 也按浏览器分开。

考试写法：Cookies are domain-specific: a browser only sends a Cookie to the domain that created it.

ex.q: mysite.net set lang=zh. User visits shop.com. Is lang sent?
ex.a: No, different domain.

ex.q: User logs in on Chrome, then opens the site on Safari. Still logged in?
ex.a: No; Safari has its own cookie store.

ex.q: 'Any website can read all my cookies.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Browsers send cookies only to the matching domain.
2. Wrong (though third-party trackers embedded on many sites can follow users).

cards.t: Benefits and potential risks of Cookies
cards.en:
Intuition: handy memory, but anyone who grabs your ticket can pretend to be you.

BenefitsRisks
Remember preferencesPrivacy: tracking browsing habits (third-party cookies)
Stay logged in (no re-typing)Cookie theft / session hijacking: stolen login cookie
Personalised contentData stored in plain text; shared computers expose it

Exam wording: Cookies improve user convenience, but may be stolen or used to track users, threatening privacy.
cards.zh:
直觉：方便的记忆，但别人拿到你的票就能冒充你。

好处风险
记住偏好私隐：追踪浏览习惯
保持登入被盗：session hijacking
个人化内容纯文字储存，公用电脑易外泄

考试写法：Cookies improve user convenience, but may be stolen or used to track users, threatening privacy.

ex.q: Why is 'remember me' convenient?
ex.a: A login cookie is sent automatically, so the user needn't type the password again.
ex.az: 自动送 cookie，不用再登入。

ex.q: Risk on a library computer?
ex.a: Next user may access the account via the stored login cookie. Log out / clear cookies.

ex.q: 'Deleting cookies makes my password stolen.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Deleting removes stored data; it reduces risk.
2. Wrong; you just have to log in again.
ex.az: 删除 cookie 只需重登，错误。

cards.en:
Intuition: never write your PIN on the ticket, and never trust a ticket the customer could have drawn themselves.

  • Don't store sensitive data (passwords, HKID numbers) in cookies: they are plain text on the client.
  • Don't trust cookie values: users can edit them, e.g. change isAdmin=0 to 1.
  • Store sensitive state on the server (sessions/database); keep only a random ID in the cookie.

Exam wording: Cookies can be read and modified by the user, so sensitive data should not be stored in them and their values must be validated on the server.
cards.zh:
直觉：别把密码写在票上，也别相信客人可自己改的票。

  • 不要存敏感数据（密码、身份证号）。
  • 不要信任 cookie 值：用户可改 isAdmin=0 为 1。
  • 敏感状态放服务器（session/数据库），cookie 只放随机 ID。

考试写法：Cookies can be read and modified by the user, so sensitive data should not be stored in them and their values must be validated on the server.

ex.q: A site stores role=student in a cookie and shows admin pages if role=admin. Problem?
ex.a: User edits the cookie to admin → gets admin access. Check role from the server database.
ex.az: 用户可改 cookie 取得权限。

ex.q: Suggest a safer design for login.
ex.a:
1. After login, server makes a random session ID.
2. Stores user info on the server.
3. Cookie holds only the session ID.
ex.az: cookie 只存随机 session ID。

ex.q: Is storing theme=dark in a cookie OK?
ex.a: Yes: not sensitive, and tampering only changes the user's own view.

cards.en:
Intuition: cookie = ticket with info written on it; session = ticket with only a number, the info stays in the shop's locker; localStorage = your own notebook the shop never asks for.

CookieSessionlocalStorage
Data kept onClientServer (ID in cookie)Client
Sent with each request?YesID onlyNo
Access$_COOKIEsession_start(); $_SESSIONJavaScript

Exam wording: Session data is stored on the server, so it is more secure than storing data in Cookies.
cards.zh:
直觉：cookie 是写着资料的票；session 是只写编号的票，资料锁在店里；localStorage 是自己的笔记本。

CookieSessionlocalStorage
存放客户端服务器客户端
每次送出是只送 ID否
读取$_COOKIE$_SESSIONJavaScript

考试写法：Session data is stored on the server, so it is more secure than storing data in Cookies.

ex.q: Store a logged-in username in a session.
ex.a: session_start(); $_SESSION["user"] = "tom";

ex.q: Save a draft note in the browser with JS.
ex.a: localStorage.setItem("note", "hi"); read with localStorage.getItem("note").

ex.q: 'localStorage data is sent to the server automatically.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Only cookies are sent automatically.
2. Wrong; JS must send it explicitly.

notes.t: Simulate localStorage with an object (runs in node)

cards.en:
Intuition: the discriminant tells you how many times the curve touches the x-axis, before you do any hard work.

  • Solve ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0).
  • Δ = b² − 4ac: Δ > 0 → two distinct real roots; Δ = 0 → one repeated real root; Δ < 0 → no real root.
  • Roots: x = (−b ± √Δ) / (2a).
  • PHP: $b ** 2, sqrt($d), and brackets around (2 * $a).

Exam wording: $d = $b ** 2 - 4 * $a * $c; then use if-elseif-else on $d.
cards.zh:
直觉：判别式先告诉你曲线碰 x 轴几次。

  • 解 ax²+bx+c=0（a≠0）。
  • Δ=b²−4ac：>0 两个不同实根；=0 一个重根；<0 无实根。
  • x=(−b±√Δ)/(2a)。
  • PHP：$b ** 2、sqrt()、(2*$a) 要括号。

考试写法：$d = $b ** 2 - 4 * $a * $c; then use if-elseif-else on $d.

ex.q: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
Classify x² + 2x + 5 = 0.
ex.a: Δ = 4 − 20 = −16 < 0 → no real root.

ex.q: Code $r = -$b / 2 * $a; with a=2, b=4 (x²-type 2x²+4x+2). Got −4, expected −1. Why?

cards.t: Quadratic Solver: one page, two kinds of request
cards.tz: Quadratic Solver：同一页处理两种请求
cards.en:
Intuition: one page acts as both the order form and the receipt.

  • quadraticSolver.php holds: Part A the form (action="", POST, a/b/c as number step="any"); Part B validation; Part C calculation and output.
  • Case 1: first visit by typing the URL → GET, no data → show the form only.
  • Case 2: click submit → POST with a, b, c, submit.
  • if (isset($_POST["submit"])) separates the cases and avoids undefined-index errors.

Exam wording: The index "submit" only exists when the user clicks the submit button, so isset($_POST["submit"]) tells whether the form has been submitted.
cards.zh:
直觉：同一页既是订单也是收据。

  • Part A 表单（action=""、POST）；Part B 验证；Part C 计算。
  • Case 1：首次输入 URL → GET，只显示表单。
  • Case 2：按 submit → POST。
  • 用 isset($_POST["submit"]) 区分。

考试写法：The index "submit" only exists when the user clicks the submit button, so isset($_POST["submit"]) tells whether the form has been submitted.

ex.q: First visit: what does the page show?
ex.a: GET request, $_POST empty → isset false → only the form.

ex.q: User submits a=1, b=−5, c=6. What appears?
ex.a: The form again, plus below it: two distinct real solutions, x = 3 or x = 2.

ex.q: A student removes the isset test and reads $_POST["a"] directly. What happens on the first visit?
ex.a:
1. No POST data.
2. Undefined index warnings and 'Invalid input!' appear before the user does anything.
3. Keep the isset check.
ex.az: 首次访问出现警告，要保留 isset。

frames.en: Typing the URL sends GET; only the form is shown.
Submit sends POST a,b,c,submit back to the same page (action="").
isset($_POST["submit"]) is true → Part B and C run; HTML with roots returned.

cards.t: Quadratic Solver Part B: validation code
cards.tz: Quadratic Solver Part B：验证代码
cards.en:
Intuition: check every input before doing maths with it.

  • For each of a, b, c: presence (empty) and type (is_numeric) checks, joined with || (OR).
  • ! means NOT.
  • Limitation: empty("0") is true, so b = 0 or c = 0 is wrongly rejected (a = 0 should be rejected anyway).
  • Improvement: for b and c test $_POST["b"] === "" instead of empty().

Exam wording: empty("0") returns true, so valid inputs of 0 for b or c are rejected.
cards.zh:
直觉：计算前先检查每个输入。

  • a、b、c 各做 presence 与 type 检查，用 || 连接。
  • ! 是 NOT。
  • 局限：empty("0") 为 true，b 或 c 为 0 被错拒。
  • 改良：b、c 用 === ""。

考试写法：empty("0") returns true, so valid inputs of 0 for b or c are rejected.

ex.q: a="1", b="x", c="2". Result?
ex.a: b fails is_numeric → $valid = false → Invalid input!

ex.q: a="0", b="2", c="1". Result and is it right?
ex.a: empty("0") → invalid. Correct, since a ≠ 0 for a quadratic.

ex.q: x² − 4 = 0 entered as a=1, b=0, c=−4. Result?
ex.a:
1. empty("0") true → $valid = false.
2. 'Invalid input!' although the equation is valid. This is a logic error; fix with === "" for b.
ex.az: b=0 被错拒，属逻辑错误。

notes.t: a missing/zero OR not a number

cards.t: Quadratic Solver Part C: calculation code
cards.tz: Quadratic Solver Part C：计算代码
cards.en:
Intuition: once data is clean, follow the maths: discriminant, then three cases.

  • $d = $b ** 2 - 4 * $a * $c;
  • if ($d > 0) two roots; elseif ($d == 0) one root; else none.
  • Output with echo and variables in {}.

Exam wording: Use sqrt() for the square root and put brackets around (2 * $a).
cards.zh:
直觉：数据没问题后照数学做：先判别式，再分三种情况。

  • 计算 $d。
  • if >0 两根；elseif ==0 一根；else 无。
  • 用 echo 与 {} 输出。

考试写法：Use sqrt() for the square root and put brackets around (2 * $a).

ex.q: a=1, b=2, c=1. Output?
ex.a: Δ = 4 − 4 = 0 → 'There is one repeated real solution. x = −1'.

ex.q: a=2, b=−3, c=1. Output?
A student writes if ($d = 0). Effect?
ex.a:
1. = assigns 0 to $d; the condition is 0 → false.
2. The repeated-root case never runs.
3. Use ==.

cards.t: Generating form fields with PHP loops
cards.tz: 用 PHP 循环生成表单字段
cards.en:
Intuition: PHP writes HTML for you, so a loop can print 40 checkboxes in 3 lines.

  • Inside a double-quoted PHP string, write a literal quote as \".
  • Process: $present = isset($_POST["present"]) ? $_POST["present"] : [];
  • $absent[] = $i; appends to the array.
  • in_array($i, $present) loosely matches 3 with "3".

Exam wording: A for loop with echo can generate repeated HTML elements.
cards.zh:
直觉：PHP 替你写 HTML，循环三行就能输出 40 个 checkbox。

  • 双引号字符串内的 " 写成 \"。
  • 没人勾时 present 不存在，先 isset。
  • $absent[] = $i 加到数组末尾。
  • in_array 宽松比较 3 与 "3"。

考试写法：A for loop with echo can generate repeated HTML elements.

ex.q: $no_of_stud = 3. What HTML does the loop produce?
ex.a: Three lines: <input type="checkbox" name="present[]" value="1"> 1<br>, then value 2, then value 3.

ex.q: 5 students; boxes 1, 2, 4 ticked. $absent?
A student writes echo "<input type="checkbox">";. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Inner " ends the string → syntax error.
2. Use \" or single quotes inside: 'checkbox'.

code.src:
{$i}
\n"; } ?>

notes.t: Print one checkbox; \" is a literal quote

code.out:
1
2
3

demo.js:
const n=5;for(let i=1;i<=n;i++)f.innerHTML+=` ${i}
`;function chk(){const p=[...f.querySelectorAll(':checked')].map(x=>+x.value);const a=[];for(let i=1;i<=n;i++)if(!p.includes(i))a.push(i);o.innerText='$absent = ['+a.join(', ')+']';}

cards.en:
Intuition: like a guard checking your name against a guest list, one line at a time.

  • Set $found = false;, loop through the list, set true if equal.
  • This is a linear search with a flag. Shortcut: in_array($x, $list).
  • Email registration: first format check (contains @), then check it is not already registered. The list lives in the server database, so this is server-side only.

Exam wording: Compare the input with each stored value in turn; if a match is found, set the flag.
cards.zh:
直觉：像保安逐行对照宾客名单。

  • $found=false，循环比较，相同则 true。
  • 这是线性查找 + flag，捷径 in_array。
  • Email 注册：先 format check，再检查未被注册。名单在服务器，只能 server-side。

考试写法：Compare the input with each stored value in turn; if a match is found, set the flag.

ex.q: $codes = ["A1","B2","C3"]; input "B2". Trace.
ex.a: A1 ≠; B2 == → $found = true; C3 ≠. Result: valid.

ex.q: Registered ["amy@a.com","bob@b.com"]; input bob@b.com.
ex.a: Format ok (@ at 3). Match found → "Email already registered".

ex.q: A student writes else { $found = false; } inside the loop. Input "A1". Result?
ex.a:
1. A1 matches → true.
2. B2 ≠ → false; C3 ≠ → false.
3. Ends false: a valid code is rejected. Remove the else.
ex.az: else 会覆盖结果，要删去。

code.src:
<?php
$codes = ["A1", "B2", "C3"];
$found = false;
foreach ($codes as $code) {
  if ($_POST["code"] == $code) { $found = true; }
}
echo $found ? "Activated" : "Invalid activation code";
?>

ex.q: Which goes in a query string?
ex.a: GET data, e.g. ?q=pen.

ex.q: Function to test 'form submitted'?
ex.a: isset($_POST["submit"]).

ex.q: 'empty() is safe for numeric fields.' Correct?
ex.a: No: empty("0") is true, so 0 is rejected.

mc.q: Where is the PHP code in a .php file executed?
mc.e: PHP is server-side: the server runs it and sends the resulting HTML.

mc.q: Which of the following does the browser receive when it requests a PHP page?
o: The resulting HTML generated by the server
mc.e: Only the resulting HTML is returned in the HTTP response.
mc.ez: 浏览器只收到结果 HTML。

mc.q: Which is a PHP web development framework?
mc.e: Laravel is for PHP; Django is Python; React/Vue are JavaScript.

mc.q: Which is NOT a benefit of using a web development framework?
o: Server-side validation is no longer needed
mc.e: Frameworks help with validation but data still must be validated on the server.
mc.ez: 框架不会令服务器验证变得不需要。

mc.q: Which statement about the <form> tag is correct?
o: It is displayed as a box on the page
Input elements must be placed inside the form tag pair to be submitted together
Its method attribute sets the file to receive the data
mc.e: All input elements must be placed within <form>...</form>.
mc.ez: 字段必须放在 form 内。

mc.q: Which attribute of <form> specifies the location to send the form's data?
mc.e: action = where the data goes.

mc.q: Which line is written correctly?
mc.e: <input> is an empty element with no closing tag.

mc.q: A text field has no name attribute. What happens when the form is submitted?
o: Its value is sent with the index "text"
Its value is sent with an empty index
It is not submitted, so the server cannot read it
The browser refuses to submit the form
mc.e: Fields without a name are not submitted.
mc.ez: 没有 name 的字段不会提交。

mc.q: Which field type obscures the user's input on screen?
mc.e: type="password" hides the characters on screen.

mc.q: Which statement about a password field is correct?
o: It encrypts the data before sending
It only hides the characters on screen
Its value cannot be read by PHP
It forces the form to use POST
mc.e: It does not encrypt; use POST and HTTPS.
mc.ez: 只在画面上遮盖，不加密。

mc.q: In what format is the value of <input type="date"> submitted?
mc.e: Date fields submit yyyy-mm-dd.

mc.q: Which attributes restrict the range of dates a user can pick in a date field?
mc.e: min and max constrain the range.

mc.q: <select name="r"><option value="KL">Kowloon</option></select>. The user picks Kowloon. What is submitted?
mc.e: The value attribute is submitted with the select's name as index.

mc.q: <select name="fruit"><option>Apple</option><option>Pear</option></select>. The user picks Pear. What is submitted?
mc.e: If value is omitted, the text between the option tags is submitted.
mc.ez: 没 value 就提交标签内文字。

mc.q: Where should the name attribute of a dropdown be placed?
mc.e: name goes on <select>.

mc.q: Why must checkboxes for one question have a name ending in [], e.g. hobby[]?
o: So that all ticked values are sent and collected as an array
To display them in a list
To make only one box tickable
mc.e: [] lets PHP collect multiple values into an array.

mc.q: A form has 3 checkboxes named lang[]; none are ticked. In the PHP script, isset($_POST["lang"]) returns:
mc.e: Unticked boxes send nothing, so the index does not exist.
mc.ez: 都没勾 → index 不存在 → false。

mc.q: <input type="submit" name="submit" value="Go!">. What does the value attribute do?
o: Sets the text displayed on the button
Sets the URL to submit to
mc.e: value changes the button's label (and is also the submitted value).

mc.q: Which attribute makes the browser block submission when a field is empty?
mc.e: required forces the user to fill in the field.

mc.q: <input type="number" name="w">. The user enters 81.3. What happens?
o: The browser blocks it because the default step is 1
mc.e: Default step is 1, so only whole numbers are valid.
mc.ez: 默认 step=1 只收整数。

mc.q: Which attribute value lets a number field accept any real number?
mc.e: step="any".

mc.q: A form must let users choose ONE delivery district from 18 fixed districts. The most suitable field is:
mc.e: Pre-defined single choice → dropdown, reduces error.

mc.q: When form data is submitted, which part becomes the index of each pair?
mc.e: name is the index; user input is the value.

mc.q: A form has no method attribute. Which method is used?
mc.e: Default is GET.

mc.q: A form has action="". Where is the data sent?
o: To the same URL as the current page
mc.e: Empty action → same URL.

mc.q: Which URL shows a correctly formed query string?
mc.e: Starts with ?, pairs index=value, separated by &.

mc.q: With POST, the form data is placed in:
mc.e: POST data goes in the request body.

mc.q: Who decides whether a form uses GET or POST?
o: The browser, based on data size
The web developer, through the method attribute
The web server, after receiving the data
mc.e: Misconception box: the developer decides.

mc.q: Which request is most suitable for GET?
o: Filtering products by brand and price
mc.e: Retrieving resources without changing the server.

mc.q: Which is a reason to use POST for a login form?
o: The password will not be shown in the address bar or saved in history
POST data is always encrypted even without HTTPS
mc.e: POST data is not visible and not bookmarked.

mc.q: Which statement about GET and HTTPS is correct?
o: With HTTPS, the request URL including the query string is encrypted during transmission
HTTPS only encrypts the request body
GET cannot be used with HTTPS
HTTPS shows the query string in plain text on the network
mc.e: HTTPS encrypts the whole request, URL included.
mc.ez: HTTPS 连 URL 都加密。

mc.q: What is the approximate maximum size of a GET query string in most cases?
mc.e: About 2KB.

mc.q: Which can be sent with POST but NOT with GET?
o: Binary data such as an image file
mc.e: GET only carries text data.

mc.q: Why can responses to GET requests be cached by a proxy server?
o: The same URL fetches the same resource, so a stored copy can be reused
GET requests have a request body
mc.e: GET fetches a resource identified by the URL.
mc.ez: 同一 URL 取同一资源可重用。

mc.q: "Sending the same request multiple times should not alter the server's state." This describes:
mc.e: Enrichment: GET is idempotent.

mc.q: A shared YouTube link opens the same video for everyone because:
o: It is a GET request whose parameters are in the URL
It is cached on the user's device
mc.e: The query string is in the URL, so it can be shared.
mc.ez: GET 参数在 URL 可分享。

mc.q: How many index-value pairs are in: book.php?id=7&lang=en&submit=go ?
mc.e: id, lang, submit.

mc.q: In PHP, POST form data is accessed through:
mc.e: $_POST superglobal.

mc.q: The URL is quiz.php?ans=B. Which PHP expression gives "B"?
mc.e: Query string data is in $_GET; index must be a string.

mc.q: A user enters 179 in a number field named height. What is the data type of $_POST["height"]?
mc.e: All form data arrives as strings.

mc.q: Checkboxes are named lang[]. Which PHP expression accesses the array of ticked values?
mc.e: The index has no brackets.

mc.q: Height 200 (cm), weight 80 (kg). $bmi = $_POST["weight"] / ($_POST["height"]/100) ** 2; What is $bmi?
What does echo "Hi {$_POST["name"]}!"; output if name is Mei?
mc.e: {} embeds the array element in a double-quoted string.

mc.q: $_POST["x"] is "7" and $_POST["y"] is "5". What does echo $_POST["x"] + $_POST["y"]; output?
mc.e: + converts numeric strings to numbers (. would concatenate).

mc.q: A form uses method="POST". The PHP page reads $_GET["name"]. What happens?
o: The index does not exist, as the data is in $_POST
It gets an empty string by design
The browser converts POST to GET
mc.e: POST data is not in $_GET.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of client-side validation?
o: It reduces the workload on the server
It can check whether a username is taken
It works the same on every browser
mc.e: It prevents most invalid data from being sent.

mc.q: Which check can ONLY be done by server-side validation?
o: Username has not already been registered
mc.e: Needs the server's database.

mc.q: Which statement is correct?
o: Use either client-side or server-side validation, not both
Client-side and server-side validation are used in parallel
Server-side validation is unnecessary if required is used
Client-side validation runs after data reaches the server
mc.e: Misconception box.

mc.q: Why should data be validated on the server even if the form has required, min and max?
o: The user can edit the HTML or send a fabricated HTTP request directly
HTML attributes slow down the browser
mc.e: Client-side validation can be bypassed.

mc.q: What does isset($_POST["age"]) return when the user submitted age as an empty string?
mc.e: The index exists (value ""), so isset is true.

mc.q: Which values make empty($x) return true?
mc.e: empty is true for missing, "", "0", 0, null, false, [].

mc.q: A user types the URL of resultBMI.php directly. The script contains echo $_POST["name"]; with no checks. What happens?
o: It shows the last name entered
A GET request is sent; the index does not exist and a runtime warning/error occurs
The browser shows the form again
mc.e: Typing the URL sends GET; $_POST is empty.

mc.q: What does strlen("Hong Kong") return?
mc.e: 9 characters including the space.

mc.q: What does strpos("tom@hk.com", "@") return?
mc.e: Positions start at 0: s0 a1 m2 @3.

mc.q: What does strpos("samhk.com", "@") return?
mc.e: Not found → false.

mc.q: Which check does in_array($_POST["size"], ["S","M","L"]) perform?
mc.e: Value must be one of a fixed set.

mc.q: Which of these makes is_numeric() return false?
mc.e: "12abc" is not a numeric string.

mc.q: $valid = true; if(empty($_POST["h"])){ $valid=false; } elseif($_POST["h"]<0 || $_POST["h"]>250){ $valid=false; }  With h = "260", $valid is:
mc.e: 260 > 250 fails the range check.

mc.q: Today is 2026-11-25. With if($_POST["d"] > date("Y-m-d")){ $valid=false; }, which d makes $valid false?
mc.e: Only a later date string is greater.

mc.q: $f = ["a","b","c"]; foreach($f as $x){ if(empty($_POST[$x])) $valid = false; } The purpose is:
o: Presence check on every expected field
mc.e: Loop presence check.

mc.q: Which validation is "email must contain @"?
mc.e: Pattern of the data → format check.

mc.q: A Cookie is best described as:
o: A file stored in the server's database
A small text file stored by a website on the client's browser
mc.e: Definition.
mc.ez: 客户端浏览器的小文本文件。

mc.q: How does a server ask the browser to create a Cookie?
o: By sending a set-cookie header in the HTTP response
By adding it to the query string
The browser creates it on its own
mc.e: set-cookie header in the response.

mc.q: Which superglobal reads Cookies in PHP?
mc.e: $_COOKIE.

mc.q: A Cookie set by abc.com is sent with:
o: every HTTP request to any domain
mc.e: Cookies are domain-specific and sent with every request to that domain.
mc.ez: 只随该 domain 的每个请求送出。

mc.q: Which is the most suitable use of a Cookie?
mc.e: Only harmless preferences.

mc.q: What is the approximate size limit of a Cookie?
mc.e: About 4KB.

mc.q: Why is storing the logged-in user ID in a Cookie a poor idea?
o: Anyone can edit the Cookie to pretend to be another user
It makes the page load slower
mc.e: Cookie values can be altered.
mc.ez: 可改 cookie 冒充他人。

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT a possible problem when a server relies on a Cookie?
mc.e: Other domains cannot read or modify it.

mc.q: In a session-based login, where is the session ID stored?
o: In the client's Cookie and in the server's database
mc.e: Saved on both sides and cross-checked.

mc.q: Which is a feature of localStorage compared with Cookies?
o: Sent to the server with every request
Much larger capacity because it is not sent with every request
It has replaced Cookies for sessions
mc.e: Enrichment box.

mc.q: For x² + 4x + 4 = 0, the discriminant and number of real roots are:
In the Quadratic Solver, why is isset($_POST["submit"]) checked?
o: To check a is not zero
The index submit only exists when the user clicks the submit button
mc.e: Distinguishes first visit (GET) from submission (POST).

mc.q: A user enters a=1, b=0, c=-9 in the book's solver, which uses empty() || !is_numeric() for each field. Output?
mc.e: empty("0") is true, so b=0 is rejected.

mc.q: Which PHP expression correctly computes one root?
mc.e: Brackets around numerator and 2a.

mc.q: Inside echo "...", how do you output a literal double quote?
mc.e: Escape with backslash.

mc.q: $a = [2]; $a[] = 5; $a[] = 9; What is count($a)?

sq.q: A school library website lets students (i) search books by title, author and year, and (ii) log in with a student ID and password to reserve books.

parts.q: State, with reasons, which HTTP request method should be used for the search form.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
GET (1)
It only retrieves data without changing the server's state / the result URL can be bookmarked or shared (1)

parts.q: State, with reasons, which method should be used for the login form.
parts.ms:
POST (1)
The password is sensitive; with POST it is not shown in the address bar or saved in browsing history/bookmarks (1)

parts.q: A student says: "GET is unsafe because the query string is sent over the Internet in plain text." Comment.
parts.ms:
Not correct if HTTPS is used (1)
HTTPS encrypts the whole HTTP request including the URL during transmission; the risk of GET is display in the address bar/history (1)

parts.q: Which request method is used? Explain.
parts.ms: GET, because the method attribute is omitted and GET is the default (1)

parts.q: Write the URL requested, assuming the page is at https://club.hk/form.html. (Ignore URL encoding of brackets.)

$registered = ["amy@a.com", "bob@b.com"];
